header: A person changes his own password (pure: the database, bcrypt, the lock, the clock and the one-time code are given by the caller, so I can test every rule without any of them). who: the SIGN-IN's ticket only (the route reads it from the session; nothing the browser says about who it is counts) proof: the current password, checked with bcrypt; wrong ones are counted and, after 5 in 15 minutes, refused outright (so a borrowed, unlocked screen cannot be used to learn the password) the HOD: during the DEVELOPMENT phase the password of the HOD of C&IT is known to two people, the HOD and the developer, and is NOT changed here (set with scripts/set-user-password.ts). When the app goes into production (APP_PHASE=production on the host) the HOD changes his own like everybody else, to what he chooses, and nobody else need know it. the new one: at least 8 characters, not the current or any of the last 5, not the ticket number, not the SAIL P.No. (the first password of everybody, which many people know), not one character repeated. the life: valid 180 days; when it has run out the window comes up by itself after sign-in, with the days in the message (src/lib/security/passwordPolicy.ts). the OTP: when PASSWORD_OTP is on, a one-time code sent to the person's own mobile (else e-mail) is needed as well (src/lib/security/otp.ts). Built; switched off. A session already open stays open until it ends (24 hours at most), because the sign-in is a signed token, not a row I can delete.

behaviours: a new password needs 8 characters, and is refused when it is the old one, the ticket, the P.No. (any case) or one repeated character
signed out: refused with 401, nothing read or written
THE HOD, in the development phase: refused (403, the plain message), the password is NOT changed, even with the right current password
the HOD's message says why and when: both people know it in the development phase; he can change it when the app goes into production
THE HOD, in production: he changes his own like everybody else, to what he chooses
what the window asks first: ordinary person yes; HOD no with the reason (development), yes (production); signed out no
only the exact word production (any case) is the production phase
a wrong current password is refused (403), counted, and nothing is written
a new password equal to the old one (the P.No.) is refused with the reason (400), nothing written
a right current password and a good new one: changed (200); a bcrypt hash of the NEW password is saved for that person's own row only
a body that is not {current, next} strings is refused (400)
an account with no password of its own (no hash) cannot be changed here (403)
an unknown ticket in the sign-in (no such row) is refused (403) and writes nothing
five wrong current passwords lock the changes (429 with a wait), even for the right one afterwards
a right current password clears the count
the route reads WHO from the session only (no ticket from the body or the address), checks the origin, and has its own failure lock and pace limiter
the route writes one row by its id, uses bcrypt cost 10, and reads the phase from APP_PHASE
the account menu has 'Change password' above Logout, and the window is drawn
the sign-in's password field is called Password and says what the first password is and where to change it
APP_PHASE is documented in .env.example
